categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's NU190x ImageSharp advisories, none introduced by the model. / returns 200 and is the blog front page via the '/' domain on the Blog page; it lists both posts newest-first as cards with cropped listing image, date, title, excerpt and 'Read post' link. Both posts render all 4 blocks (rich text, image with caption, rich text, quote) with no render errors. All 4 images are provided Unsplash photos imported into a 'Blog Images' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs that load. All content published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock, quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages; siteRoot stays the only root type and allows only blogFrontPage, which allows only blogPost. Templates assigned (default + allowed). One custom 'Blog Block Grid' data type (12 columns, the three blocks) filed under Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid and used as 'body' on both page types. Post metadata (title, publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties; no compositions, no duplicate or orphaned types. Aliases camelCase.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both page views call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body"); scaffold blockgrid partials untouched; no custom loops. Three adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models in Models/Blocks/ and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup (a using alias resolves the clash with Umbraco's own RichTextBlockModel). Three one-line ViewComponents render Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml, which depend only on the plain models. Program.cs/appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, friendly Children<T>/Url()/GetCropUrl, Tailwind built into wwwroot/dist/site.css. Small deduction: both page views carry a full duplicated HTML shell (Layout = null, same head/footer) and the post's 'All posts' link is hard-coded to '/' rather than the parent's Url().

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic posts ('One Protocol, Every Tool' and 'Editors Get Superpowers Too'), ~370-400 words each over 6 paragraphs and 4 blocks, with relevant network/code imagery and credited captions. The writing is accurate in general, but it's on the short side, and post 2 says 'The front page you are reading' and 'not through hand-edited files' (the Razor was hand-written), so −0.5. Presentation is clean and coherent: a header with intro, a two-column card grid, a readable narrow post column with styled figure and blockquote, and a consistent footer.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: 53 MCP calls across umbraco (schema, media, domain) and umbraco-editor (pages, blocks, publish); no Management API, DB, uSync writes, browser or migrations. Followed the order: model → content → stop/build → Razor → restart. Stayed in the project folder, no memory access, and removed its scratch HTML files. The final report is accurate: it describes what was built, the RichTextBlockModel ambiguity fix and the publish-order hiccup, and claims nothing untrue.

summary: A clean, fully working MCP-built blog: three well-formed blocks (rich text, image, quote) on a shared block grid, front page with image/date/excerpt cards and two published posts, rendered through the exact adapter → ViewComponent pipeline with Tailwind styling. Only nitpicks: duplicated page shells, a hard-coded back link, and slightly short posts with one inaccurate line.
strengths: Every automated check passes (43/43); build clean apart from scaffold package warnings
Textbook block pipeline: alias-named adapters, plain models in Models/Blocks, one ViewComponent per block, GetBlockGridHtmlAsync on both pages
Correct schema: types in the right folders, tight allowed children, real post metadata, one custom block grid in /Custom
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served via GetCropUrl, with no repeats

issues.text: Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and Views/blogPost.cshtml each set Layout = null and duplicate the full HTML head/footer shell
Views/blogPost.cshtml hard-codes the 'All posts' link to '/' instead of using the parent page's Url()
/why-mcp-is-awesome-editors-get-superpowers-too/ says 'The front page you are reading' and claims nothing was hand-edited; both posts are fairly short (~400 words)
